subject.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk

question: Should OpenClaw retain trajectory tool-call records on every reset under the existing reset archive retention policy, and should this combined PR supersede the reset-only implementation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593?
rationale: The code is mechanically sound, but reset preservation intentionally extends the lifetime of sensitive tool arguments/results and two viable PRs currently encode that policy at different ownership boundaries.

options.title: Approve the combined lifecycle
options.body: Use this PR as the canonical delete/reset/rollover implementation, require exact-head proof, and close the overlapping reset-only PR after landing.

options.title: Keep reset policy separate
options.body: Narrow this PR to delete and writer-race safety while retaining https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593 for a separate reset-retention decision.

options.title: Do not retain on reset
options.body: Remove reset tombstoning from both branches and keep trajectory deletion on reset while landing only the delete-orphan repair.

recommendation.title: Approve the combined lifecycle
recommendation.body: Use this PR as the canonical delete/reset/rollover implementation, require exact-head proof, and close the overlapping reset-only PR after landing.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the live assignee and authored the lifecycle invariant that drove the current architecture.
